domain: Political Economy / Economic History / Institutional Analysis
topic_summary: Analysis of the claim that 'the market is the natural default' economic arrangement, examining whether this represents a lapsed-alternative naturalization (no active maintenance required) or a beneficiary-maintained construction (incumbents defend it post-hoc). The kernel contest centers on whether market dominance is a D3 artifact requiring engineered closure or a lapsed closure that persists without active defense.

key_entities: The Market (claimed as natural default economic coordination mechanism)
State Apparatus (enforcer of property rights, contract law, monetary system)
Incumbent Capital Holders (beneficiaries of current property distribution)
Alternative Coordination Systems (commons, gift economies, planned economies, mutual aid)
Naturalization Discourse (rhetorical apparatus claiming market as pre-political)
key_tensions: Natural vs Constructed (market as discovered vs engineered institutional arrangement)
Lapsed vs Maintained (closure requiring no defense vs active beneficiary protection)
key_mechanisms: Property Rights Enforcement (state violence backing ownership claims)
Enclosure Processes (conversion of commons to private property)
Ideological Reproduction (education, media, economic theory naturalizing market logic)
key_absences: Historical Contingency (specific conditions enabling market dominance)
Maintenance Costs (resources required to sustain market institutions)

commitment_system_recognition.kernel_description: The market as natural default economic arrangement
commitment_system_recognition.authority_description: Economic theory, policy institutions, and property law claiming to describe rather than prescribe coordination mechanisms

readings.commitment: Market dominance is a lapsed closure requiring no active maintenance
readings.authority_grounding: Evolutionary economics, spontaneous order theory, efficiency claims
readings.expected_structural_delta: No identifiable beneficiary class; alternatives atrophied through non-use; low extractiveness (coordination costs only)

readings.commitment: Market dominance is actively defended by incumbent capital holders
readings.authority_grounding: Historical materialism, institutional economics, power analysis
readings.expected_structural_delta: Identifiable beneficiary class (capital holders); active suppression of alternatives; high extractiveness (rents + enforcement costs)

readings.commitment: Market dominance combines lapsed elements with active maintenance
readings.authority_grounding: Institutional path dependency, political economy synthesis
readings.expected_structural_delta: Mixed beneficiary structure; some alternatives lapsed, others suppressed; moderate extractiveness (varies by domain)

axes.structural_delta: Market dominance persists because alternatives atrophied through non-use, not active suppression
axes.primary_observable: Absence of identifiable enforcement mechanisms targeting non-market coordination; historical record of alternative system decline without state intervention
axes.selection_reason: First reading of contested kernel; tests whether market naturalization is coordination mechanism without beneficiary structure

axes.structural_delta: Market dominance requires active defense by capital holders through state apparatus and ideological reproduction
axes.primary_observable: Identifiable enforcement spending (police, courts, IP law); lobbying expenditures; enclosure history; suppression of alternative experiments
axes.selection_reason: Second reading of contested kernel; tests whether market naturalization is extractive construction requiring maintenance

axes.structural_delta: Market dominance combines genuinely lapsed elements with actively maintained components varying by domain
axes.primary_observable: Domain-specific variation in enforcement intensity; differential survival rates of alternative systems by sector
axes.selection_reason: Third reading of contested kernel; tests whether market naturalization is heterogeneous across institutional domains

axes.structural_delta: Property rights enforcement as unavoidable coordination cost in any economic system
axes.primary_observable: Cross-system comparison of enforcement costs; transaction cost economics
axes.selection_reason: Deferred: upstream to all readings but kernel contest centers on maintenance structure, not base coordination costs

axes.structural_delta: Specific historical mechanisms converting commons to private property
axes.primary_observable: Enclosure Acts, land privatization records, indigenous dispossession documentation
axes.selection_reason: Deferred: historical evidence for beneficiary_maintained_reading but kernel contest is synchronic (current maintenance structure)

axes.structural_delta: Educational and media systems naturalizing market logic
axes.primary_observable: Economics curriculum content; media ownership concentration; think tank funding
axes.selection_reason: Deferred: evidence for beneficiary_maintained_reading but kernel contest is institutional structure, not discourse

omegas.description: Does maintenance structure vary systematically by domain (finance vs agriculture vs digital goods)? Hybrid reading predicts heterogeneity but lacks domain-specific decomposition.

omegas.description: How to distinguish lapsed closure from successfully concealed maintenance? Absence of visible enforcement may indicate either genuine lapse or effective naturalization.
omegas.source: Dark Matter Probe 2 (Absence Inventory) + lapsed_alternative_reading observable

omegas.description: Are contemporary alternative experiments (cooperatives, commons, mutual aid) suppressed or simply uncompetitive? Empirical test requires controlling for scale and network effects.

omegas.description: Do the three readings share a genuine common substrate or are they incommensurable frameworks? Lapsed reading denies beneficiary existence; beneficiary-maintained reading requires it. Hybrid reading may be conceptual compromise rather than structural synthesis.

fracture_scan.notes: No fractures detected. Kernel decomposition successfully identified three structurally distinct readings with different beneficiary structures and epsilon bins. Omega_kernel_coherence flags potential incommensurability between readings for downstream analysis.
